title: A 15-minute phone-free walk
why: Gentle movement plus daylight is one of the most reliable mood lifters there is.

title: Desk stretch break every 90 minutes
why: Long hours sitting tighten your neck and shoulders, which your brain reads as tension.

title: Beginner yoga (20 min, YouTube is fine)
why: Combines breath, stretch and focus — great for busy minds.

title: Try a boxing or kickboxing class
why: A healthy outlet for frustration that leaves you calmer afterwards.

title: Dance to 3 songs in your room
why: Silly, private and surprisingly effective at shaking off a heavy mood.

title: Join a casual sports group (badminton, football)
why: Exercise and friendship in one — two of the strongest protectors of mental health.

title: Digital sunset: no screens 45 min before bed
why: Blue light and endless feeds keep your brain switched on when it's trying to sleep.

title: Build a 3-step wind-down ritual
why: Same steps every night (tea, dim lights, a page of reading) teach your body it's time to rest.

title: A 20-minute power nap (before 3 pm)
why: Short naps restore alertness without wrecking your night's sleep.

title: Write 3 good things before bed
why: Gratitude journaling trains your attention to notice what's going right.

title: Morning brain-dump: 1 page, no editing
why: Getting loops of thought onto paper frees up mental space for the day.

title: 5-minute daily meditation streak
why: Small daily practice beats occasional long sessions for building calm.

title: Sketch one object around you
why: Drawing slows you down and pulls your attention into the present.

title: Try watercolour or colouring pages
why: Low-pressure art with no 'wrong' outcome is deeply calming.

title: Make a playlist for each mood you feel
why: Knowing which songs lift or calm you gives you a tool for hard moments.

title: Learn 3 chords on an instrument
why: Learning music gives you a sense of progress and absorbs your focus completely.

title: Cook a dish from a cuisine you've never tried
why: Cooking is hands-on, sensory and ends with a reward.

title: Grow a small plant or herb
why: Caring for something living gives a gentle daily routine and quiet pride.

title: Get 10 minutes of morning sunlight
why: Morning light sets your body clock, boosting energy by day and sleep by night.

title: Join a book club (online or local)
why: Turns a solo hobby into connection with people who think like you.

title: Call (not text) one friend this week
why: Hearing a familiar voice is far more connecting than messages.

title: Volunteer for a cause you care about
why: Helping others is one of the most consistent boosters of wellbeing.

title: Host a board game or co-op game night
why: Keeps the fun of gaming but adds face-to-face connection.

title: Study/work in 25-minute Pomodoros
why: Short focused sprints with breaks beat long, guilt-filled sessions.

title: Plan tomorrow in 3 priorities, tonight
why: Deciding tonight removes morning overwhelm and decision fatigue.
